text: Post-harvest handling of vegetables (ការគ្រប់គ្រង និងការរក្សាទុកបន្លែក្រោយប្រមូលផល) should focus on keeping produce cool, clean, undamaged, and marketable for the shortest practical time. Harvest during a cooler part of the day when practical, move produce into shade immediately, and avoid leaving full containers in direct sun -- this matters most during the hot dry season (រដូវប្រាំង), while the wet season (រដូវវស្សា) adds problems from rain, mud, excess surface moisture, and decay. Sort before packing: separate rotten, diseased, leaking, or badly damaged produce immediately, since damaged produce accelerates deterioration of nearby vegetables. Washing should NOT be automatic -- without clean, safe water and appropriate follow-up handling, washing can introduce contamination or leave produce wet, increasing decay; ask whether the produce is actually dirty and whether clean water is available before recommending washing. Use clean, sturdy containers without packing so tightly that vegetables are crushed or lack ventilation. Do not assume cold-chain infrastructure is available -- refrigerated storage and specialized packaging may suit high-value produce for distant markets but should not be presented as a normal requirement for a farmer selling locally. The realistic smallholder chain is: shade -> ventilation -> gentle handling -> rapid sale, rather than assuming refrigerated storage. Ask 'who will buy the vegetables and how far will they travel?' since that substantially changes handling and packaging needs. Do not name one universal 'best' vegetable variety for Preah Vihear -- ask the farmer which vegetable and variety they're growing before giving crop-specific handling advice.
